syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Individual Differences and Assessment of Psychological Attributes
topics.ncert_sections: Individual Differences in Human Functioning; Assessment of Psychological Attributes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain individual differences and how situationism accounts for behaviour through situational factors.
Identify the domains of intelligence, aptitude, interest, personality and values.
Distinguish formal from informal assessment and the methods of test, interview, case study, observation and self-report.

topics.title: Intelligence and Psychometric Theories
topics.ncert_sections: Intelligence; Theories of Intelligence

concepts.learning_objective: State how Binet, Wechsler and later theorists defined intelligence.
Describe the one-factor, two-factor, primary mental abilities, hierarchical and structure-of-intellect theories.

topics.title: Multiple Intelligences, Triarchic Theory and the PASS Model
topics.ncert_sections: Theory of Multiple Intelligences; Triarchic Theory of Intelligence; PASS Model of Intelligence

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Gardner's eight independent intelligences and the persons typically high on each.
Distinguish componential, experiential and contextual intelligence in Sternberg's theory.
Explain arousal/attention, simultaneous and successive processing, and planning in the PASS model.

topics.title: Nature, Nurture and the Measurement of IQ
topics.ncert_sections: Intelligence: Interplay of Nature and Nurture; Assessment of Intelligence

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret twin and adoption evidence on heredity and environment in intelligence.
Calculate IQ from mental age and chronological age, and mental age from IQ.
Interpret the normal distribution of IQ scores and the classification in Table 1.1.

topics.title: Variations of Intelligence
topics.ncert_sections: Variations of Intelligence: Intellectual Deficiency; Intellectual Giftedness

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the AAMD definition and the levels of intellectual disability.
Distinguish giftedness from talent and describe how gifted children are identified.

topics.title: Types of Intelligence Tests and Testing in India
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Intelligence Tests; Some Misuses of Intelligence Tests (Box 1.1); Intelligence Testing in India

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish individual and group, verbal, non-verbal and performance, and culture-fair and culture-biased tests.
Recognise the ill-effects of intelligence testing by untrained testers.
Identify pioneering efforts and tests in intelligence testing in India.

topics.title: Culture, Intelligence and Emotional Intelligence
topics.ncert_sections: Culture and Intelligence; Intelligence in the Indian Tradition; Emotional Intelligence

concepts.learning_objective: Compare technological intelligence with non-western views and Vygotsky's view of culture.
Describe integral intelligence, buddhi and the competencies valued in the Indian tradition.
Explain emotional intelligence and the characteristics of emotionally intelligent persons.

topics.title: Aptitude and Creativity
topics.ncert_sections: Special Abilities: Aptitude: Nature and Measurement; Creativity; Creativity and Intelligence

concepts.learning_objective: Explain aptitude, how it differs from interest, and how independent and multiple aptitude tests measure it.
Explain variations in creativity and the roles of heredity and environment.
Evaluate the relationship between creativity and intelligence and how creativity tests differ.

topics.title: Concept of Self
topics.ncert_sections: Concept of Self; Self as Subject and Self as Object; Kinds of Self

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish personal identity from social identity using a person's self-descriptions.
Explain the dual status of the self as a subject (knower) and as an object (known).
Describe the biological, personal and social (relational) self and how they emerge.

topics.title: Cognitive and Behavioural Aspects of Self
topics.ncert_sections: Self-concept; Self-esteem; Self-efficacy; Self-regulation

concepts.learning_objective: Define self-concept and self-esteem and relate self-esteem to behaviour and parenting.
Explain self-efficacy, its basis in Bandura's social learning theory and how it develops.
Apply the techniques of self-regulation and self-control to everyday situations.

topics.title: Culture and Self
topics.ncert_sections: Culture and Self

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the Indian and Western views of the boundary between self and other.
Relate individualistic and collectivistic cultures to the way self and group are related.

topics.title: Concept of Personality
topics.ncert_sections: Concept of Personality; Box 2.1 Personality-related Terms

concepts.learning_objective: State the origin and psychological meaning of the term personality.
Identify the main features of personality and use them to understand and deal with people.
Distinguish temperament, trait, disposition, character, habit and values.

topics.title: Type and Trait Approaches
topics.ncert_sections: Type Approaches; Trait Approaches; Box 2.2 Five-Factor Model

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the typologies of Hippocrates, Charak Samhita, Sheldon, Jung and Friedman and Rosenman.
Explain the trait theories of Allport, Cattell and Eysenck.
Interpret a personality description in terms of the Big Five factors.

topics.title: Psychodynamic Approach
topics.ncert_sections: Psychodynamic Approach; Post-Freudian Approaches

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Freud's levels of consciousness, structure of personality and stages of development.
Identify ego defence mechanisms such as repression, projection, denial, reaction formation and rationalisation.
Describe the contributions of Jung, Horney, Adler, Fromm and Erikson.

topics.title: Behavioural, Cultural and Humanistic Approaches
topics.ncert_sections: Behavioural Approach; Cultural Approach; Humanistic Approach; Box 2.3

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the behavioural approach views personality as learnt responses to the environment.
Explain personality as an adaptation to the ecological and cultural demands of a group.
Explain Rogers' real and ideal self and Maslow's idea of self-actualisation.

topics.title: Assessment of Personality
topics.ncert_sections: Assessment of Personality; Self-report Measures; Projective Techniques; Behavioural Analysis

concepts.learning_objective: Describe MMPI, EPQ and 16PF and the problems of self-report measures.
Explain the assumptions, features and examples of projective techniques.
Describe interview, observation, ratings, nomination and situational tests and their limitations.

topics.title: Nature of stress
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Nature, Types and Sources of Stress; Nature of Stress

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish eustress from distress and explain stress as a pattern of responses to demands that exceed coping ability.
Explain Lazarus's primary and secondary appraisal and the harm, threat and challenge appraisals of an event.
Describe stress reactions and how intensity, duration, complexity and predictability shape the outcome of stress.

topics.title: Types and sources of stress
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Stress; Sources of Stress; Box 3.1

concepts.learning_objective: Identify physical and environmental, psychological and social stress with examples.
Explain frustration, conflict, internal pressure and social pressure as sources of psychological stress.
Distinguish life events, daily hassles and traumatic events and interpret life event measures of stress.

topics.title: Effects of stress on psychological functioning
topics.ncert_sections: Effects of Stress on Psychological Functioning and Health; Box 3.2

concepts.learning_objective: Classify emotional, physiological, cognitive and behavioural effects of stress.
Explain how examination anxiety can help or impair a student's performance.
Define burnout as a state of physical, emotional and psychological exhaustion.

topics.title: Stress and health
topics.ncert_sections: Stress and Health; General Adaptation Syndrome; Stress and the Immune System; Lifestyle

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the alarm reaction, resistance and exhaustion stages of Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome.
Explain how stress impairs the immune system, as studied by psychoneuroimmunology.
Analyse how stress leads to health-damaging lifestyle behaviours.

topics.title: Coping with stress
topics.ncert_sections: Coping with Stress

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the task-oriented, emotion-oriented and avoidance-oriented coping strategies of Endler and Parker.
Differentiate problem-focused and emotion-focused coping as described by Lazarus and Folkman.

topics.title: Stress management techniques
topics.ncert_sections: Stress Management Techniques

concepts.learning_objective: Describe relaxation, meditation and the stages of biofeedback training.
Explain the aim and phases of Meichenbaum's stress inoculation training.
Explain how creative visualisation and exercise help to manage stress.

topics.title: Hardiness and life skills
topics.ncert_sections: Promoting Positive Health and Well-being; Life Skills

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Kobasa's stress resistant personality and its three Cs: commitment, control and challenge.
Identify life skills such as assertiveness, time management, rational thinking, improving relationships and self-care.
Recognise perfectionism, avoidance and procrastination as unhelpful habits that increase vulnerability to stress.

topics.title: Factors promoting positive health
topics.ncert_sections: Box 3.3; factors facilitating positive health

concepts.learning_objective: Explain resilience and its I HAVE, I AM and I CAN resources.
Explain how diet, exercise, positive attitude and optimism act as stress buffers.
Distinguish tangible, informational and emotional social support and explain their effect on well-being.

topics.title: Concepts of abnormality and historical background
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Concepts of Abnormality and Psychological Disorders; Historical Background

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the four Ds (deviance, distress, dysfunction, danger) common to definitions of psychological disorders.
Distinguish the view of abnormality as deviation from social norms from the view of abnormality as maladaptive behaviour.
Trace the supernatural, biological and psychological perspectives on abnormal behaviour through history to the bio-psycho-social approach.

topics.title: Classification of psychological disorders
topics.ncert_sections: Classification of Psychological Disorders; Activity 4.2

concepts.learning_objective: State the features of DSM-5 (American Psychiatric Association) and ICD-10 (World Health Organisation).
Explain why classifying psychological disorders is useful to professionals.
Evaluate why the situation in which a behaviour occurs matters in judging it as abnormal.

topics.title: Factors underlying abnormal behaviour
topics.ncert_sections: Factors Underlying Abnormal Behaviour

concepts.learning_objective: Relate genetic and neurotransmitter factors to specific psychological disorders.
Explain abnormal behaviour using the psychodynamic, behavioural, cognitive and humanistic-existential models.
Apply the socio-cultural model and the diathesis-stress model to explain the onset of disorders.

topics.title: Anxiety, obsessive-compulsive and trauma-related disorders
topics.ncert_sections: Anxiety Disorders; Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders; Trauma- and Stressor-Related Disorders

concepts.learning_objective: Identify generalised anxiety disorder, panic disorder and separation anxiety disorder, and when anxiety becomes a disorder.
Distinguish specific phobias, social anxiety disorder and agoraphobia.
Distinguish obsessions from compulsions and recognise the symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder.

topics.title: Somatic symptom and dissociative disorders
topics.ncert_sections: Somatic Symptom and Related Disorders; Dissociative Disorders; Box 4.1

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish somatic symptom disorder, illness anxiety disorder and conversion disorder.
Describe dissociative amnesia, fugue, dissociative identity disorder and depersonalisation/derealisation disorder.

topics.title: Depressive and bipolar disorders; suicide
topics.ncert_sections: Depressive Disorders; Bipolar and Related Disorders; Suicide

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the symptoms of and risk factors for major depressive disorder.
Describe bipolar I disorder and the related disorders in this category.
Evaluate risk factors for suicide and measures for identifying and helping students in distress.

topics.title: Schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders
topics.ncert_sections: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders

concepts.learning_objective: Classify delusions, formal thought disorders, hallucinations and inappropriate affect as positive symptoms.
Distinguish negative symptoms (alogia, blunted affect, avolition) from psychomotor symptoms such as catatonia.

topics.title: Neurodevelopmental, conduct, eating and substance-related disorders
topics.ncert_sections: Neurodevelopmental Disorders; Disruptive, Impulse-Control and Conduct Disorders; Feeding and Eating Disorders; Substance-Related and Addictive Disorders

concepts.learning_objective: Describe ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability and specific learning disorder.
Identify features of oppositional defiant disorder, conduct disorder and the eating disorders.
Explain tolerance, withdrawal and the effects of alcohol, heroin and cocaine.

topics.title: Nature and process of psychotherapy and the therapeutic relationship
topics.ncert_sections: Nature and Process of Psychotherapy; Therapeutic Relationship

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the characteristics and goals shared by all psychotherapeutic approaches.
Explain the components and unique properties of the therapeutic alliance, including unconditional positive regard.
Distinguish empathy from sympathy and intellectual understanding.

topics.title: Types of therapies and clinical formulation
topics.ncert_sections: Type of Therapies; Box 5.1

concepts.learning_objective: Compare psychodynamic, behaviour and existential therapies on the parameters used to classify them.
Explain the advantages of clinical formulation of a client's problem.

topics.title: Behaviour therapy
topics.ncert_sections: Behaviour Therapy; Box 5.2

concepts.learning_objective: Identify malfunctioning behaviours, antecedent and maintaining factors, and establishing operations.
Apply techniques such as reinforcement, aversive conditioning, token economy and differential reinforcement.
Explain systematic desensitisation, reciprocal inhibition and relaxation procedures.

topics.title: Cognitive therapy and cognitive behaviour therapy
topics.ncert_sections: Cognitive Therapy; Cognitive Behaviour Therapy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Ellis's ABC analysis and the disputing of irrational beliefs in RET.
Describe Beck's account of core schemas, critical incidents and negative automatic thoughts.
Explain the bio-psychosocial rationale of cognitive behaviour therapy.

topics.title: Humanistic-existential therapies
topics.ncert_sections: Humanistic-existential Therapy; Existential Therapy; Client-centred Therapy; Gestalt Therapy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how frustration of self-actualisation causes distress and how humanistic therapy heals.
Describe Frankl's logotherapy and the process of meaning making.
Describe the techniques and goals of client-centred and gestalt therapy.

topics.title: Factors contributing to healing and ethics in psychotherapy
topics.ncert_sections: Factors Contributing to Healing in Psychotherapy; Ethics in Psychotherapy

concepts.learning_objective: Identify techniques, therapeutic alliance, catharsis and non-specific factors as contributors to healing.
State the ethical standards to be practised by professional psychotherapists.

topics.title: Alternative therapies
topics.ncert_sections: Alternative Therapies

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish yoga, focused meditation and Vipasana meditation as alternative therapies.
Describe research findings on SKY, Kundalini Yoga and mindfulness-based meditation.

topics.title: Rehabilitation of the mentally ill
topics.ncert_sections: Rehabilitation of the Mentally Ill

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why rehabilitation is needed when symptom reduction does not improve quality of life.
Distinguish occupational therapy, social skills training, cognitive retraining and vocational training.

topics.title: Nature and Components of Attitudes
topics.ncert_sections: Nature and Components of Attitudes; Box 6.1

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the affective, behavioural (conative) and cognitive components of an attitude and how far they agree.
Distinguish an attitude from a mere opinion and from actual behaviour.
Distinguish attitudes from beliefs and values.

topics.title: Features of Attitudes
topics.ncert_sections: Nature and Components of Attitudes (Valence, Extremeness, Simplicity or Complexity, Centrality)

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the valence and extremeness of an attitude from ratings on a scale.
Explain simple and complex (multiplex) attitude systems with member attitudes.
Explain the role of a central attitude within an attitude system.

topics.title: Attitude Formation
topics.ncert_sections: Attitude Formation: Process of Attitude Formation; Factors that Influence Attitude Formation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain learning of attitudes by association, reward and punishment, modelling, group norms and exposure to information.
Describe how family and school, reference groups, personal experiences and media shape attitudes.

topics.title: Process of Attitude Change
topics.ncert_sections: Attitude Change: Process of Attitude Change; Box 6.2

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Heider's P-O-X triangle to judge balance and imbalance.
Explain Festinger's cognitive dissonance and the Festinger and Carlsmith experiment.
Describe Mohsin's two-step concept of attitude change through identification and imitation.

topics.title: Factors that Influence Attitude Change
topics.ncert_sections: Attitude Change: Factors that Influence Attitude Change

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how properties of the existing attitude and the direction of change affect attitude change.
Analyse how source, message and target characteristics influence attitude change.

topics.title: Attitude-Behaviour Relationship
topics.ncert_sections: Attitude-Behaviour Relationship

concepts.learning_objective: State the conditions under which attitudes and behaviour are consistent, with LaPiere's study.
Explain how behaviour can sometimes decide the attitude.

topics.title: Prejudice and Discrimination
topics.ncert_sections: Prejudice and Discrimination

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish stereotype, prejudice and discrimination as components of attitudes towards a group.
Identify the sources of prejudice such as learning, ingroup bias, scapegoating, kernel of truth and self-fulfilling prophecy.

topics.title: Strategies for Handling Prejudice
topics.ncert_sections: Strategies for Handling Prejudice

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the aims and strategies for handling prejudice.
Evaluate the conditions under which intergroup contact reduces prejudice.

topics.title: What is a group: characteristics, and groups versus crowds, teams, audiences and mobs
topics.ncert_sections: Nature and Formation of Groups: What is a Group?

concepts.learning_objective: Define a group and identify its salient characteristics such as interdependence, roles, norms and a sense of belonging.
Distinguish groups from crowds, teams, audiences and mobs.

topics.title: Why do people join groups?
topics.ncert_sections: Why Do People Join Groups?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how groups satisfy needs for security, status and self-esteem.
Explain how groups help in goal achievement, satisfy social needs and provide knowledge and information.

topics.title: Group formation and Tuckman's stages of group development
topics.ncert_sections: Group Formation; Stages of Group Formation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how proximity, similarity and common motives and goals facilitate group formation.
Describe Tuckman's stages of forming, storming, norming, performing and adjourning and recognise them in real groups.

topics.title: Group structure: roles, norms, status, cohesiveness and groupthink
topics.ncert_sections: Stages of Group Formation (group structure); Box 7.1 Groupthink

concepts.learning_objective: Explain roles, norms and ascribed versus achieved status as elements of group structure.
Explain group cohesiveness and why extreme cohesiveness may not be in a group's interest.
Describe groupthink, the conditions that favour it and ways to prevent it.

topics.title: Types of groups and the minimal group paradigm
topics.ncert_sections: Type of Groups; Box 7.2 The Minimal Group Paradigm Experiments

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish primary groups from secondary groups.
Distinguish formal groups from informal groups.
Explain ingroup and outgroup perceptions and interpret Tajfel's minimal group paradigm.

topics.title: Social facilitation and social loafing
topics.ncert_sections: Influence of Group on Individual Behaviour: Social Loafing

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish social facilitation from social loafing and describe Latane's findings.
Explain why social loafing occurs on collective tasks.
Suggest ways of reducing social loafing in groups.

topics.title: Group polarisation
topics.ncert_sections: Group Polarisation

concepts.learning_objective: Define group polarisation and predict its effect on group decisions.
Explain the three reasons why group polarisation occurs.
